nodes.description: Lymphatic capillaries are normally free of mural cells. In FOXC2 deficiency a large proportion of dermal lymphatic vessels acquire pericytes and smooth muscle cells, a defect seen in skin biopsies from patients as well as in mice. Dermal lymphatic vessel density is not reduced in patients.

nodes.description: FOXC2 and PROX1 are highly expressed in the endothelial cells that form lymphatic valves. Together with flow they induce connexin37 and calcineurin/NFAT signaling, which delimit the valve territory and drive maturation of the primary lymphatic plexus into valved collecting vessels. Foxc2-null mice have no lymphatic valves, and postnatal lymphatic deletion of Foxc2 causes valve regression and junctional defects, so FOXC2 is needed both to build and to maintain the valves.

evidence.reference_title: Defective valves and abnormal mural cell recruitment underlie lymphatic vascular failure in lymphedema distichiasis.
evidence.snippet: We report that Foxc2(-/-) mice show abnormal lymphatic vascular patterning, increased pericyte investment of lymphatic vessels, agenesis of valves and lymphatic dysfunction.

evidence.reference_title: Mechanotransduction, PROX1, and FOXC2 cooperate to control connexin37 and calcineurin during lymphatic-valve formation.
evidence.snippet: Mechanistically, PROX1, FOXC2, and flow coordinately control expression of the gap junction protein connexin37 and activation of calcineurin/NFAT signaling.

evidence.reference_title: FOXC2 controls formation and maturation of lymphatic collecting vessels through cooperation with NFATc1.
evidence.snippet: In this study, we provide a molecular and morphological characterization of the major steps in the maturation of the primary lymphatic capillary plexus into collecting lymphatic vessels during development and show that forkhead transcription factor Foxc2 controls this process.

evidence.reference_title: FOXC2 and fluid shear stress stabilize postnatal lymphatic vasculature.
evidence.snippet: In murine models, inducible deletion of Foxc2 within the lymphatic vasculature led to cell-cell junction defects, regression of valves, and focal vascular lumen collapse, which triggered generalized lymphatic vascular dysfunction and lethality.

evidence.reference_title: Foxc2 is expressed in developing lymphatic vessels and other tissues associated with lymphedema-distichiasis syndrome.
evidence.snippet: We have found that Foxc2 is expressed in lymphatic primordia, jugular lymph sacs, lymphatic collectors and capillaries, as well as in podocytes, developing eyelids and other tissues associated with abnormalities in lymphedema-distichiasis syndrome.

evidence.reference_title: Mechanotransduction activates canonical Wnt/β-catenin signaling to promote lymphatic vascular patterning and the development of lymphatic and lymphovenous valves.
evidence.snippet: In turn, Wnt/β-catenin signaling controls the expression of several molecules, including the lymphedema-associated transcription factor FOXC2. Importantly, FOXC2 completely rescues the lymphatic vessel patterning defects in mice lacking β-catenin.

evidence.reference_title: Truncating mutations in FOXC2 cause multiple lymphedema syndromes.
evidence.snippet: FOXC2 appears to be the primary cause of lymphedema-distichiasis syndrome and is also a cause of lymphedema in families displaying phenotypes attributed to other lymphedema syndromes.

nodes.description: Nonsense, frameshift and other truncating FOXC2 variants, and a translocation breakpoint downstream of the gene that inactivates it by position effect, reduce the dose of active FOXC2, a forkhead-box transcription factor. Variants in the forkhead DNA-binding domain and central region reduce transactivation. A minority of missense variants outside the forkhead domain instead increase transactivation in reporter assays, so altered FOXC2 activity in either direction can perturb lymphatic development, but loss of function is the established mechanism.

evidence.snippet: In two additional unrelated families with LD, we identified inactivating mutations-a nonsense mutation and a frameshift mutation-in the FOXC2 (MFH-1) gene.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in FOXC2 (MFH-1), a forkhead family transcription factor, are responsible for the hereditary lymphedema-distichiasis syndrome.
evidence.snippet: Our findings show that FOXC2 haploinsufficiency results in LD.

evidence.snippet: Our data reveal that either a complete loss or a significant gain of FOXC2 function can cause a perturbation of lymphatic vessel formation leading to lymphedema.

nodes.description: Distichiatic lashes grow from the meibomian gland orifices, reflecting a metaplastic switch of the meibomian (tarsal) sebaceous glands into pilosebaceous units. Foxc2 is expressed in the developing eyelid and Foxc2 heterozygous mice uniformly have distichiasis. A reporter study suggests FOXC2 variants reduce activation of the WNT4 promoter, which has been proposed, but not shown in vivo, to link FOXC2 loss to the gland-to-follicle switch.

nodes.description: Spinal extradural arachnoid cysts protrude into the epidural space through a dural defect and can compress the cord. All reported familial cases are associated with LDS, and a cyst can be the only manifestation in a FOXC2 carrier. In one large family, 7 of 12 carriers had cysts on spinal MRI, but the frequency across families is unknown, so no frequency band is assigned. Syndromic cysts tend to be multiple and to extend beyond the thoracolumbar region.

nodes.description: FOXC2 is highly expressed on venous valves. FOXC2 carriers have pathological reflux in the great saphenous vein and often in the deep veins, including carriers without lymphedema, which indicates primary venous valve failure rather than a consequence of the lymphedema.
